newsitem.title: JAPAN: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Oct 29.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Oct 29.

text.p: Nihon Cement Co Ltd plans to set up a joint venture to produce and sell light heat-resistant auto parts in cooperation with Akebono Brake Industry Co Ltd and trading house Kanematsu Corp. It hopes to build plants in Japan and southeast Asia, and targets annual sales of five billion yen in five years. The venture, to be capitalised at 490 million yen, will be owned 45 percent each by Nihon Cement and Akebono and 10 percent by Kanematsu.

Ford Motor Co and General Motors Corp are planning to issue bonds in Japan for the first time through local finance affiliates, hoping to benefit from low-cost financing in Japan. The issues are likely to be yen/dollar dual-currency bonds. Ford plans to issue more than 30 billion yen worth of bonds, targetting individual investors, in November. The three-year issue will be lead-managed by Nomura Securities Co Ltd. General Motors plans to issue about three billion yen worth of such bonds by the end of this year.

Bridgestone Corp has reached an agreement with a leading South African conglomerate to acquire all shares in Fedstone PTY Ltd, a holding company which owns South Africa's second-largest tyre manufacturer. The purchase cost will be about 7.2 billion yen. As a result, Bridgestone will have a share of about 25 percent in the South African tyre market.

Pharmaceutical company Sankyo Co Ltd is expected to have posted record parent current profit of around 50 billion yen in the half year to September 30, up 13 percent from the same period a year earlier, helped by strong sales of its medical products.

Unitika Ltd is expected to have posted parent current profit of 1.7 billion yen in the half year to September 30, down from a projection of two billion yen. The company's sales are expected to have been 150 billion yen for the half-year period.
